claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gunplay as clunky, floaty, and outdated.

citations.review_text:
I went into Black Squad hoping for a solid, no-frills military shooter, and it saddens me to say it just didn’t hit the mark. Ultimately, most of the negative reviews floating around on Steam make sense from where I’m sitting.

The shooting mechanics feel oddly floaty instead of grounded, and teamplay is rarely encouraged by the gameplay. The maps are uninspired, with repetitive layouts and little variety, leaving every match feeling like a copy-and-paste experience. On top of that, the balance is painfully off, some guns feel borderline overpowered, while others barely register hits. It doesn’t feel like skill is properly rewarded.

I also noticed the monetization system leans very heavily on cosmetics and premium items. It never outright blocked me from fair matches, but there’s a clear advantage in having that premium equipment, something that shouldn’t be this prominent in a competitive shooter.

At its core, Black Squad has a cool name and a nostalgic vibe, but the execution feels unfinished. Between inconsistent gameplay mechanics, flat maps, and a paywall-heavy approach, it doesn’t live up to what it promises. Not the worst FPS out there, but also not one I'd recommend for long, especially when other free shooters offer a more polished and balanced experience.

Gunplay feels clunky and outdated. Optimization is terrible; expect constant frame drops even on good hardware. A lot of the maps are uninspired and encourage camping. Plenty of other free-to-play shooters do everything it attempts, but better. Overall, it's disappointing.

Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3/5)

Black Squad is a free-to-play tactical FPS that tries to capture the essence of classic military shooters, but it doesn’t fully live up to its potential. The core gameplay offers solid mechanics with responsive shooting and a decent variety of weapons, giving players an experience that’s easy to pick up. The game has its moments of fun, especially in team-based modes, where strategy and coordination can turn the tide of a match. The maps are fairly well-designed and diverse, providing enough variety to keep matches feeling fresh.

However, the game struggles with balancing issues, especially with weapon damage and movement mechanics. While it’s fun in short bursts, the lack of depth in progression and customization makes it hard to stay invested for the long term. The graphics are decent, but they don’t stand out compared to other FPS titles. There are also issues with microtransactions, which, while not essential to enjoy the game, can feel a bit intrusive.

Overall, Black Squad delivers an average tactical shooter experience, but it doesn’t do anything particularly unique to set itself apart from the crowd. It’s fun for a quick match or two, but it doesn’t have the staying power of other more polished FPS titles.

Pros:

Solid core gameplay and responsive shooting.

Decent variety of maps and modes.

Free-to-play, making it accessible to many players.

Cons:

Balancing issues with weapons and movement.

Lack of depth in progression and customization.

Microtransactions feel intrusive.

Graphics don’t stand out.

Verdict:
Black Squad is a decent tactical FPS that offers short bursts of fun, but it falls short in terms of long-term engagement and polish. It’s worth trying if you’re looking for a free-to-play shooter, but it doesn’t quite stack up against more refined FPS titles.

citations.review_text:
I came into this game expecting another generic free-to-play shooter, but it actually kept me playing much longer than I expected.

The gameplay is where Black Squad shines. Gunfights are fast, movement feels responsive, and getting a clean headshot is incredibly satisfying. It has that old-school FPS feeling that reminds me of the days when shooters focused more on mechanics than flashy abilities. Matches are easy to jump into, and earning new weapons without spending money is a nice bonus.

The game also deserves credit for not forcing players to pay for power. You can enjoy everything that matters through gameplay, which is becoming increasingly rare in free-to-play games.

Unfortunately, after putting in more hours, the cracks start to show. The biggest issue is the lack of long-term support. Cheaters still appear often enough to ruin competitive matches, updates feel more focused on cosmetics than improving the core experience, and some technical problems have existed for years. It's frustrating because the gameplay itself is genuinely fun.

The player base isn't as healthy as it used to be either, so matchmaking can sometimes feel unbalanced, especially if you're looking for a serious competitive experience.

That said, if you're searching for a free FPS that mixes classic Counter-Strike style gunplay with faster Call of Duty pacing, this is still worth trying. Just don't expect it to become your forever shooter.

Overall: 7.5/10

✔ Fun and responsive gunplay
✔ No pay-to-win mechanics
✔ Easy to get into
✘ Cheaters hurt the experience
✘ Weak long-term support
✘ Missed potential

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features a large selection of maps, weapons, and game modes like Team Deathmatch and Demolition.

citations.review_text:
Black Squad is a free military FPS that feels like it is trying to keep things simple and fast. I can jump into a match, pick a weapon and get straight into the shooting without having to learn a huge amount of stuff first. The game has been around since 2019, but it still gets updates and new content, so it does not feel completely stuck in the past. I like that it gives me a fairly traditional FPS experience instead of trying to turn every match into some massive progression system.

The amount of actual content is probably the strongest thing for me. There are 10 game modes including Competitive, Demolition and Team Deathmatch, along with 48 maps and more than 85 weapons covering rifles, SMGs, shotguns, snipers, pistols and LMGs. I can also create custom games when I want to mess around with different settings. That gives me quite a lot to play with, especially considering the game itself is free. I like having a big selection of weapons because it lets me change how I play instead of getting stuck using the same type of gun every match.

The shooting itself is where I think Black Squad works best. I can focus on aiming, movement and learning the maps without having to worry about a complicated ability system. Competitive and Demolition give me more structured matches when I want something serious, while Team Deathmatch is easier to jump into when I just want to shoot things for a while. There are also ranked and clan based options, so I have somewhere to take the game if I decide I want to play it more seriously. The recent updates also show that the game is still being maintained, with new weapons, temporary modes and events being added.

The free to play setup is something I am more mixed about. The game says that everything can be earned through playing, which I like, but there are still in game purchases and chance based purchases. There are also hundreds of weapon and character skins, so a lot of the progression is tied into collecting and customising rathe…

Black Squad is a solid free‑to‑play FPS with fast-paced gunplay and a nice variety of maps and modes. Unlocking weapons and skins is fair — you can get most things just by playing, no pay-to-win grind. The playerbase is relatively small, but during peak hours matches are easy to find, so you can still jump in without long waits.

Игра Black Squad - это динамичный и хардкорный шутер от первого лица, который явно вдохновлен классикой жанра. Подкупает большой выбор оружия, каждое из которых ощущается по-своему, а также множество режимов игры, от классического Deathmatch до тактических операций. Графика вполне достойная, хоть и не хватает современных технологий.

Однако, главным минусом является порог вхождения. Новичкам придется потратить много времени, чтобы освоиться и начать конкурировать с опытными игроками. Баллистика требует привыкания, а знание карт критически важно. Также, наблюдаются проблемы с оптимизацией и стабильностью серверов, хотя разработчики активно работают над их устранением.

В целом, Black Squad - это крепкий шутер, который может увлечь любителей хардкорного геймплея и тактических перестрелок. Если вы готовы потратить время на освоение и простить некоторые недостатки, то игра может стать отличной альтернативой более популярным проектам. Но помните, легкой прогулки не будет.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game runs well and features low system requirements, making it suitable for low-end PCs.

citations.review_text:
An Excellent, Fast-Paced Military FPS That Runs Well on Any PC!
With nearly 50 hours on record, this game remains one of the best free-to-play tactical shooters for anyone looking for fast, fluid, and action-packed gameplay.

Solid and Responsive Gunplay: The weapon handling feels incredibly smooth. The recoil patterns are easy to pick up yet rewarding to master, making every single firefight feel deeply satisfying.

Fast-Paced Action: Unlike slower tactical shooters, this game delivers quick, intense, and straightforward military combat that keeps you on your toes.

Superb Optimization: The game runs exceptionally well and is highly optimized. It’s perfect for players who want a competitive FPS experience without needing a high-end gaming rig.

A fantastic choice for some casual or competitive fun, especially when looking to squad up with friends. Highly recommended! 8.5/10.

Black Squad is an FPS with around 150-300 daily players — a small but consistent community.

The game offers a set of stable modes (TDM / Demolition [S&D] + more)
New players get the chance to earn some permanent skins along with a ton of crates… though 99% of the time, those crates won’t give you anything permanent. Money will.... maybe. 

The game runs smoothly and has quite low system requirements. 
Movement is somewhat acceptable. Weapon recoil takes a lot of getting used to — it’s not exactly friendly for newcomers.
No overpowered utilities, no crazy weapon models — just a straightforward shooter experience.

Many of the remaining veteran players are a real challenge skill-wise, which can easily become frustrating. It’s hard not to suspect that some of them might be using recoil scripts. 

-rep for the takeover by VALOFE, although to be fair, the game had already outlived its natural lifespan by then.

Despite its age and flaws, Black Squad is a game that brings me back to the old nonesense CS days — even if the two games are worlds apart.
Great Game for Low-End PC's

citations.review_text: Should've sold my items before steam trade disappeared

It had great potential to become the next big FPS shooter—until they messed up every update. First, they removed the tradable and marketable item systems. Second, they handed the game over to another company (I think), and that’s when things got ruined by cheaters. There’s been no progress in updates for competitive matches, and the game is flooded with cheaters. On top of that, they merged all the servers, which made it super laggy. That’s why I sadly stopped playing the game.

citations.review_text: Ass game. The devs did a really good job at the beginning when it was in its early access phase several years ago. That's when it got a bit popular. There was a solid player base as the gameplay was smooth with fewer glitches and bugs. But once the devs noticed the popularity they immediately shifted their 100 percent focus (that's right literally their full focus) on ♥♥♥♥♥♥ shiny cosmetics and microtransactions. Basically no features or further improvements were made and to make things worse, they outright stopped fixing bugs and glitches properly. The game literally broke as time passed and now its still getting messier. The game had huge potential on its own but unfortunately the devs got greedy and ruined it. This game means a lot to me as it has years of special memories and I would absolutely love to see it get better but seeing how things are going it's not a good sign at all.
